content.text: June's stated total is €300 below the sum of its own line items (158,240 vs 158,540 — May and July reconcile exactly, so this looks like a typo in the bold total). I'll use the line-item sum as authoritative and flag it. Computing the rest:

input.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP

def pct(x):  # one decimal place, half-up
    return float(Decimal(str(x)).quantize(Decimal('0.1'), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))

rev  = {'may':412380, 'jun':431205, 'jul':389640}
cost = {'may':151120, 'jun':158540, 'jul':158280}   # jun = line-item sum
new  = {'may':86, 'jun':74, 'jul':63}
churn= {'may':17, 'jun':22, 'jul':31}
op   = {'may':342, 'jun':361, 'jul':298}
cl   = {'may':315, 'jun':350, 'jul':291}

q_rev  = sum(rev.values())
q_cost = sum(cost.values())
q_net  = q_rev - q_cost

out = {
  "q_revenue_eur": q_rev,
  "q_costs_eur": q_cost,
  "q_net_eur": q_net,
  "margin_pct": pct(q_net / q_rev * 100),
  "net_customer_adds": sum(new.values()) - sum(churn.values()),
  "ticket_close_rate_pct": pct(sum(cl.values()) / sum(op.values()) * 100),
  "june_revenue_growth_pct": pct((rev['jun'] - rev['may']) / rev['may'] * 100),
  "july_revenue_growth_pct": pct((rev['jul'] - rev['jun']) / rev['jun'] * 100),
  "notes": ("June's stated total costs (EUR 158,240) do not match the sum of its own cost "
            "line items (EUR 158,540), a EUR 300 shortfall; May and July reconcile exactly, "
            "so the June bold total appears to be a typo and the line-item sum is used here. "
            "Using June's stated total instead would give q_costs_eur 467,640, q_net_eur 765,585 "
            "and margin_pct 62.1. Also of note: July revenue fell 9.6% month-on-month while "
            "churn rose each month (17 to 22 to 31), so net adds declined from 69 in May to 32 in July."),
}
print(json.dumps(out, indent=2))
with open('RESULTS.json','w') as f:
    json.dump(out, f, indent=2)
    f.write('\n')
print("\n--- unrounded checks ---")
print("margin", q_net/q_rev*100)
print("close",  sum(cl.values())/sum(op.values())*100, sum(cl.values()), sum(op.values()))
print("jun g",  (rev['jun']-rev['may'])/rev['may']*100)
print("jul g",  (rev['jul']-rev['jun'])/rev['jun']*100)
PY
